descriptionChirho: To propel something through the air with force; physical throwing or casting of objects such as stones, nets, or people into locations (sea, fire, prison), including figurative casting (seed, fire upon earth).
Passive or middle voice: to be thrown, cast, or hurled into a place (sea, fire, Gehenna, prison), often expressing divine judgment or violent removal.
To place or deposit something into a container or location without forceful propulsion; putting money into the treasury, putting wine into wineskins, placing a bit in a horse's mouth.
To be lying down prostrate, typically of a sick person bedridden or an object lying in a place; used of those found lying ill or cast down in weakness.
To pour a liquid substance onto or into something, as ointment on the head or new wine into wineskins.
Of wind or natural forces striking or beating against something; the wind beat upon that house.
To expel or drive out forcefully, especially of casting out demons or removing something unwanted; to cause to fall or drop.
